findings.how: Round 1: engine.ts skips the barge-in transcript under 0.1 s. sherpa.ts transcribe() returns "" under 0.1 s and reports a recognizer throw through onError. process.ts catches throws out of feed()/feedMonitor() and sends engine-error, at most once a minute. Round 2 (verifier, failures were swallowed without limit): failures are now bounded. More than 20 within 10 s mark the recognizers unusable (a WebAssembly abort or out-of-memory error leaves them so). The voice process then sends {type:'engine-broken'} once and stops feeding them. VoiceService logs voice.engine_broken and calls restartLater("The speech recognizer kept failing."), so the 1/5/30 s backoff applies and the restart loads fresh models. Failures spread out over time never count as broken.

findings.how: Round 1: while this computer's screen is locked, VoiceService stops listening and speaking, askEmber refuses and maySpeak is false. Round 2 covers the verifier's six points. (1) The gate is at the desktop itself. lockedOutHands (screen-lock.ts) wraps this screen's hands so that, while locked, every perception and sidecar read or step rejects with "This computer's screen is locked, so Ember didn't read it or act on it." and currentWindow() is null. This also covers WSL apps' windows, which are on this screen. The borrowed mouse's input is lockAwareInput(xinput, …), so CursorBorrow's screenLocked() check is true whenever ScreenLock says locked, including GNOME's lock shield. The 2-s sweep is now a backstop. In addition, screenHands (targets/hands.ts) now implements DesktopUse per task (a read, a step, an app opened, the desk). Locking stops only tasks that used the screen, and a task running only commands goes on, as docs §4.4 already said; before, every running local task was stopped because local hands couldn't say. (2) A wrong 'locked' reading. On Linux, initial() is no longer trusted: Ember starts unlocked, and only a logind read that says locked locks it, so a first read that can't tell leaves it unlocked. graphicalSession() uses XDG_SESSION_ID only when its Type is x11, wayland or mir, and otherwise the user's Display session, so a terminal's or SSH session that is never in front can't pin Ember as locked. A request refused while locked shows "Your screen is locked, so I didn't take that." (3) The onChange body is now LockController (inject stopDesktopTasks, setLocked and showNotice), unit-tested. (4) The notice is shown through holdNotice: claimBubble, then after 8 s, if still showing, releaseBubble(notice), and the bubble is hidden only if that returns false. A running task shows its progress again at once. The refusal bubble uses the same helper. (5) There is no process every 2 s. One `gdbus monitor --system --dest org.freedesktop.login1 --object-path /org/freedesktop/login1/session/<escaped id>` (LC_ALL=C) runs for the whole session, and loginctl is read only on a PropertiesChanged line or when the watch begins. If gdbus is missing or exits, loginctl is read every 5 s; with no graphical session nothing is watched. stop() kills the watcher on quit. Checked here against real gdbus and a private bus: it stays up and is killed on stop, and with no bus it falls back. Not done: stopping that fallback poll while Ember is idle (it only runs without gdbus, which glib2 ships). WSL tasks aren't stopped on lock (their screen use is refused by the gate; their commands go on). docs/COMMANDS-WSL-SSH.md §4.4 is updated.
findings.test: test/unit/screen-lock.test.ts, 30 tests, all failing on bf22035^ (23 of them; the rest are the kept parse cases). They cover the gdbus watch (one monitor, reads only on PropertiesChanged or when the watch begins, none in 60 s otherwise), the 5-s fallback when gdbus is missing or stops, 'starts unlocked, whatever Electron says…' (the old code stayed locked with initial true and a poll returning null) and the graphical-session choice and session-path escaping. They cover LockController's four cases (lock stops tasks and starts the sweep; sweep stops count; unlock notice once with singular/plural, sweep cleared; nothing stopped says nothing) and holdNotice (release after 8 s, hide only when nothing else shows, a replaced notice left alone). They also cover lockedOutHands (every read and step refused while locked, untouched while unlocked) and lockAwareInput. targets-hands.test.ts adds 'tell whether their own task used this screen…'. Round 1: the ScreenLock and VoiceService lock tests.

forDocs: CHANGELOG: "Speak replies, questions and results out loud" is now a choice: When a screen reader runs (default), Always, or Never. Never keeps Ember quiet even while a screen reader runs. An organisation that turns speaking off shows it as Never (managed).

CHANGELOG: While this computer's screen is locked, or another session is in front, Ember doesn't listen for "Hey Ember", doesn't speak, takes no requests ("Your screen is locked, so I didn't take that.") and doesn't read or act on the screen. Tasks that used the screen stop, and are reported once you're back. A task running only commands goes on.
Install docs (Linux): lock detection uses logind through `gdbus` (glib2, installed with GNOME on RHEL 8). Without gdbus, Ember reads loginctl every 5 s.

CHANGELOG: Where Ember can't tell its own voice from yours (Windows, macOS, and Linux without parec), spoken announcements name the stop shortcut ("Press Windows key, Alt, X to cancel.") instead of "Say 'Ember, stop'".

CHANGELOG: Damaged speech models show "The speech models look damaged. Download them again.", and the download button repairs them. Models installed with Ember are never changed: the download goes to your own models folder.
CHANGELOG: A microphone that sends only silence (muted, or the wrong input) is now reported instead of "Listening for 'Hey Ember'".
CHANGELOG: The model download shows "Unpacking speech models… N%" after the last byte, instead of sitting at 100%.

CHANGELOG / install docs (Linux): speaker rejection follows the default sound output when it changes (pactl from pulseaudio-utils, as for parec). While Ember listens, it keeps the output device from idle-suspending.
CHANGELOG: The voice process restarts by itself when it stops responding or its recognizer keeps failing, using the 1/5/30 s backoff.
ciOnly: RHEL 8 GNOME: with Ember running, Super+L makes `gdbus monitor --system --dest org.freedesktop.login1 --object-path /org/freedesktop/login1/session/_3N` print a PropertiesChanged line for LockedHint, and Ember logs screen.lock {locked:true}. Unlocking logs locked:false, and switching users or VTs (Active=no) does the same. The audit log shows no periodic loginctl execve.
RHEL 8: Ember started from a terminal or an SSH login's session reads the user's graphical session (Type check) and is not stuck 'locked'.
RHEL 8 GNOME lock shield: a task's accessibility reads and borrowed input are refused while locked (lockedOutHands, lockAwareInput), and a local commands-only task keeps running across a lock.
Windows/macOS: powerMonitor lock-screen/unlock-screen and getSystemIdleState(1)==='locked' at start. The unlock notice gives the bubble back after 8 s, so a running task's progress shows again.

RHEL 8 PulseAudio 14: after switching the default sink (headphones, Bluetooth), `pactl list short source-outputs` shows parec on the new sink's monitor. Changing only the default input leaves parec's source-output id unchanged.
Windows/macOS with speakers and a microphone: a spoken announcement names the stop shortcut and no longer triggers the kill switch (#251).
Windows/macOS spawn latency: a voice process stopped before 'spawn' is killed once it spawns (#256).
A signed macOS Ember.app, or a per-user Windows install, with a damaged bundled model folder: the bundle is untouched, and the download repairs into the user's models folder (#254).

verifierProblems.what: A damaged bundled model folder gets its markers deleted, and the next download is written into the app's own install folder. voiceModelsRoot() (main.ts:156) hands VoiceService a bundled root (Ember.app/Contents/Resources/voice-models on macOS, resources\voice-models on Windows from --with-models builds, /usr/share/ember/voice-models, %ProgramData%). On a models:true error, voice.ts:293 calls forgetModels(this.o.modelsRoot). For a writable bundle, such as a drag-installed Ember.app owned by the user or a per-user Windows install, the .ok markers are removed and the state goes to needs-models with 'Download them again.'. downloadModels() then runs ensureModels(this.o.modelsRoot), so about 110 MB goes into the signed app bundle on macOS (the seal is broken, and updates replace it). Only the read-only case was handled.
verifierProblems.fix: Pass `bundled` (speechModels.bundled) into VoiceOptions. For a bundled root, never call forgetModels on it: switch the service's models root to the user's own folder (path.join(userData, 'models')) and go to needs-models there, so the download repairs it outside the bundle. Or, if that's too wide a change, show the reinstall error. Add a voice-service test with a bundled root that asserts its markers stay and the download targets the user folder.

verifierProblems.what: Failures are now swallowed without limit. process.ts `failed()` counts every throw out of feed()/feedMonitor() and reports one engine-error a minute, and VoiceService only logs it (voice.ts:300). A recognizer that fails on every frame stays deaf for the rest of the session while the UI says 'Listening for “Hey Ember”', and there is no restart: for example, a WebAssembly abort or out-of-memory error leaves the module unusable. Before the fix, that crash restarted the process with fresh models through restartLater.
verifierProblems.fix: Bound it. In process.ts, when failures keep coming (say more than 20 in 10 s, or N frames in a row), exit with code 1 or send a new {type:'engine-broken'}, so VoiceService calls restartLater('The speech recognizer kept failing.') and the backoff applies. Add a voice-process test (spot throws on every frame: one exit/report after the threshold) and a voice-service test (restart scheduled).

verifierProblems.what: Local tasks can still use the desktop for up to 2 s while the screen is locked. cancelTasksOn('local','desktop') skips queued tasks, and running tasks whose taskDesktop() is still false (host.ts:1415). A queued local task that starts while the screen is locked can read the screen or send input until the next 2-s sweep. On Linux, the local hands' own lock check (hands/input.ts XScreenSaver/DPMS) doesn't see GNOME's lock shield, so typed input in that window can land in the lock screen's password field. This is not a regression (nothing stopped before), but the gate is at the wrong layer.
verifierProblems.fix: Gate the desktop itself while screenLock.locked. Give the local hands a screenLocked() that is true when ScreenLock says so (a one-line OR in the input package's check, coordinated with the input package), or hold queued local tasks while locked and release them on unlock. Then the sweep is only a backstop.

verifierProblems.what: A wrong 'locked' reading makes Ember ignore the user silently. askEmber drops every request while locked with only a log line (main.ts:757), and the voice line says 'Not listening while the screen is locked.'. On Linux there is no unlock event, and a poll that can't tell keeps the last state (screen-lock.ts tick). If initial() (powerMonitor.getSystemIdleState(1)==='locked') says locked at start and loginctl is unavailable or fails, Ember stays 'locked' until it restarts. The same happens if logind reports Active=no for the session id Ember inherited. Typed requests then do nothing, with no message.
verifierProblems.fix: On Linux, when a poll is configured, don't take initial() as authoritative: start unlocked, or only trust 'locked' once a poll confirms it. Treat a first poll that can't tell as unlocked. When askEmber refuses because of the lock, show a short bubble, e.g. 'Your screen is locked, so I didn't take that.'. If the user can see it, the detection was wrong, and they learn why nothing happened.

verifierProblems.what: The main.ts lock wiring has no test. The onChange handler (voice.setLocked, desktop-task sweep every 2 s, the unlock notice counted once and reset), askEmber's refusal and maySpeak's lock clause are covered only by typecheck and the smoke test, which never locks.
verifierProblems.fix: Move the onChange body into a small controller in app/main/screen-lock.ts (inject cancelTasks, setLocked and showNotice). Unit-test four cases: lock stops desktop tasks and starts the sweep; a sweep while locked adds to the count; unlock shows the notice once with the right singular/plural and clears the sweep; a lock/unlock with nothing stopped shows nothing.

verifierProblems.what: After an unlock, the notice holds the bubble longer than it shows. main.ts:1650 calls agent.claimBubble() (a 30 s MAIN_HOLD_MS) and hides the notice after 8 s, but never releases the claim. A commands-only or remote task still running then shows no progress for about 22 s after the notice goes.
verifierProblems.fix: Release the claim when the notice ends, as main.ts:886-893 do. Replace hideIfStill(bubble, 8000) with a timer that, if the notice is still showing, calls `if (!(agent?.releaseBubble(bubble) ?? false)) setState({ emotion: 'neutral', bubble: IDLE_BUBBLE })`.

verifierProblems.what: The Linux lock poll starts a new process every 2 s for the whole session (`loginctl show-session …` from main, screen-lock.ts:89), about 43,000 runs a day. On RHEL 8 machines that audit execve, which is common in the enterprises Ember targets, every run is logged.
verifierProblems.fix: Use one long-lived watcher instead of polling: `gdbus monitor --system --dest org.freedesktop.login1 --object-path /org/freedesktop/login1/session/<id>` (glib2 ships it on RHEL 8 GNOME). Re-read LockedHint/Active on each PropertiesChanged, and fall back to polling only if gdbus is missing. If polling stays, use a longer interval (5-10 s) and stop it while Ember has nothing listening or running.

verifierProblems.what: When the organisation manages speaking, the label no longer dims. #speak is now a <select> beside a <label for>, not inside a <label>. home/main.ts:328 does `(input.closest('label') ?? input).classList.toggle('locked', …)`, so the opacity 0.5 lands on the select only. 'Speak replies, questions and results out loud' stays at full strength while its control is disabled, unlike the other managed rows.
verifierProblems.fix: Use `input.closest('label, .choice') ?? input` in that loop, so the whole .choice row gets `locked`.

verifierProblems.what: Docs are stale. docs/DEVELOPING.md:129 still says '**Speak replies** on (or a screen reader running) it says the question out loud', but speaking is now a three-way choice where Never wins over a screen reader. The README/CHANGELOG need the docs package to know about the new choice.
verifierProblems.fix: Update DEVELOPING.md:129, e.g. 'With Speak … out loud set to Always, or a screen reader running and it set to When a screen reader runs (the default), it says the question out loud', and list the new choice in the report for the docs package.

verifierProblems.what: Unverified, and broader than needed. speakers.ts restarts parec on every `Event 'change' on server`, which also fires when the default input changes and, under pipewire-pulse, for other server-level changes. Each restart is a short gap in the speakers' stream (the replaced run isn't reported off). Nothing here proves the new parec actually lands on the new sink's monitor: there is no PulseAudio in this container.
verifierProblems.fix: On a server change, read the default sink (`pactl info`, 'Default Sink:' line; RHEL 8's PulseAudio 14 has no get-default-sink) and restart parec only when it differs from the last one. Before release, verify on RHEL 8 hardware with `pactl list short source-outputs` after switching sinks, as the reviewer asked.
